draft.title: Budgeting
card: A budget is a plan for the money you expect to earn and spend. List all income, such as wages, then list all expenses.
an expense that stays the same each period, such as rent or a phone plan with a set price.
an expense that changes from one period to the next, such as food or petrol.
Savings = income − expenses. Example: Zoe earns $900 a fortnight. Rent is $400 and food is $150. Other costs are $200. Expenses are $750, so she can save $900 − $750 = $150.
draft.remember: A budget compares income with expenses. What is left over can be saved.

a.q: Which of these is a variable cost for a household?
opts: Groceries, which change from week to week
Rent of $350 a week for a unit
A gym membership of $20 a fortnight
A car loan repayment of $200 a month
a.why: Groceries change in amount from one period to the next, so they are variable. The rent, membership and loan repayment are set amounts, so they are fixed costs. Rent is the most tempting wrong option, but it stays the same each week.
a.clue: Which cost would not be the same amount each time?

b.q: Liam earns $1200 a fortnight. His expenses are rent $520, food $210, transport $90 and other costs $180. How much can he save each fortnight?
b.why: Expenses are 520 + 210 + 90 + 180 = $1000. Savings = 1200 − 1000 = $200. Giving $1000 is a mistake, because that is the total of the expenses, not what is left.
b.clue: Add up every expense first, then subtract from income.

a.best: Groceries, which change from week to week

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier, and that qualifier ('which change from week to week') restates the card's definition of a variable cost. A student can pick it without knowing the idea. Use plain 'Groceries' or give every option a similar description.

check.summary: Facts and arithmetic are correct (Zoe saves $150, Liam saves $200). Question a gives its answer away, because the correct option is the only one that includes the definition 'which change from week to week'.
